title: Standby briefing — ZenPay priority outage (prep notes)
content:
Purpose: quick prep for standby ops brief with CS + SRE + Serving runtime. This is a scratchpad — not polished. Goal: align on initial triage, customer comms cadence, and immediate mitigations we can try before full war-room.

Context / background:
- Customer: ZenPay (payment orchestration). Large traffic on eu-west region. Reported degraded response times and intermittent 500s for calls to /v1/generate since ~2026-03-12T22:10UTC.
- Impact: elevated P50 -> 700ms (baseline 120ms), error rate increased to ~6% of requests in last 30m, payments UI shows timeouts for <5% users but high business-critical risk.
- Recent changes: autoscaler tweak rolled 2026-03-12 20:50 by infra (PR #987) that adjusted batch sizing thresholds for long-context models.

Attendees (proposed):
- Rohit (CS lead, primary customer contact)
- Leah (SRE, incident lead)
- Marco (serving-runtime eng)
- Tess (platform + routing)
- Optionals: Priya (account manager), Hana (security)

Pre-brief checklist (things to confirm before opening war-room):
- [ ] Confirm customer contact chain + preferred cadence (already DM'ed Priya).
- [ ] Capture last 60m logs for zenpay-api-key (k=vz-zenpay-*) and store snapshot link.
- [ ] Verify deploys in eu-west in last 24h (infra PRs, release-engineering notes).
- [ ] Check if fallback model variants were engaged (model routing trace).
- [ ] Reserve Zoom + doc for war-room and mark calendar (15m heads-up).

Quick signals to check in first 10m:
- Recent deploys: `git log --pretty=oneline -n 5 origin/main` (repo: runtime)
- Autoscaler events: `kubectl get hpa -n inference -o yaml` and check metrics server anomalies
- Error spike fingerprints: sample stacktraces from logs -> route to Marco if related to kernel selection/quantization path
- Model-specific policy: confirm whether request routing fell back to smaller quantized variant (Q4_0) and whether that introduced new codepath.

Immediate mitigation options (fast tries):
1) Route ZenPay traffic to a compatible older model variant (rollback routing) for a 15–30m mitigation window. Pros: immediate; Cons: potential quality regressions. Implementation: Tess to flip routing policy in control plane (requires 2m).
2) Disable continuous batching temporarily (forcing small batch path) to reduce backend latency tail if batching causing long wait. Marco + Leah to coordinate.
3) Increase dedicated capacity for zenpay shard (burst to dedicated pool) — needs approval but can be enacted by platform.
4) Fallback to cached prefix (if applicable) for high-frequency prompts — ask customer for example prompt prefixes.

Customer comms:
- Initial message (within 10m of war-room start): short acknowledgment + ETA for next update (30m). Rohit to send on the ZenPay thread: "We're investigating increased latency/500s affecting a subset of requests. Engineering is in a standby brief now; next update in 30m or sooner. Attach link to war-room doc."
- Update cadence: 30m updates until stable, then hourly.
- Escalation path: Priya -> CSM director if >2 hours unresolved or >10% user impact sustained.

Draft war-room agenda (20–30m):
- 0–5m: current signal summary + owner alignment (Leah)
- 5–10m: recent deploys & infra checks (Marco/Release)
- 10–15m: mitigation decision + action owners (Tess/Marco/Leah)
- 15–20m: comms draft + customer-facing ETA (Rohit)
- 20–30m: next steps and handoff (if not resolved -> escalate)

Notes / hypotheses (raw):
- Hypothesis A: autoscaler/batching change created pathological queueing for odd sequence lengths -> latency tail. Evidence: changes in PR #987 mention batch thresholds.
- Hypothesis B: new kernel selection path on quantized model introduced a memory hotspot -> occasional OOMs leading to 500s. Check OOM/kube events.
- Hypothesis C: network flapping between eu-west AZs causing increased tail; check route53 and infra monitoring.

Commands/queries to run (for SRE):
- `kubectl get pods -n inference -l customer=zenpay -o wide`
- `kubectl logs -n inference --tail=200 deployment/infer-zenpay | egrep "ERROR|OOM|timeout|stacktrace"`
- Query APM: service:inference env:eu-west metric:latency 95p, group by model_variant

Decision criteria (how we'll pick mitigations):
- If error rate is >3% and latency P95 >1.5s: immediate routing rollback to previous model variant.
- If OOMs present: scale up or reduce batch size, prioritize stability.
- If no infra or model code errors and traffic pattern spike: throttle or shard customer traffic to dedicated pool.

Post-meeting action items (capture in linear/Jira and update here):
- ACTION 1: Tess -> flip routing to previous variant (if approved). Owner: Tess. Due: 2026-03-13 00:00 UTC. Ticket: JIRA-4523.
- ACTION 2: Marco -> instrument additional kernel-level logs and attach sample traces. Owner: Marco. Due: 2026-03-13 01:00 UTC. Ticket: JIRA-4524.
- ACTION 3: Leah -> collect k8s events + heap/oom logs and post to doc. Owner: Leah. Due: 2026-03-12 23:45 UTC. Ticket: JIRA-4525.
- ACTION 4: Rohit -> customer update + timeline. Owner: Rohit. Due: 2026-03-12 23:30 UTC.
- ACTION 5: Priya -> standby exec brief if >1h outage. Owner: Priya. Due: as needed.

Open questions (to ask in war-room):
- Did ZenPay push any change from their side around 20:45? (ask customer)
- Are there matching spikes in other customers in eu-west? (SRE telemetry)
- Can we reproduce with load test? (Marco)

Wrap-up notes (scratch):
- Keep this doc minimal and time-stamped updates only. Post-resolution: write an RCA skeleton (owner: Marco) and a customer-facing summary (owner: Rohit).
- If routing rollback helps, follow-up: schedule root-cause deep-dive and revert only after a fix.

Scratch log (timestamps are local notes):
- 22:12: noticed P50 jump; p95 trending upward.
- 22:18: Leah confirmed error count rising; requested SRE join.
- 22:22: Marco checking PR #987 for batch changes.

End of prep scratchpad. Use for war-room kickoff. Update this file during war-room and then create a cleaned RCA in shared_drives/company/misc after resolution.
